title: Treaty (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Treaties''' allow two Civilizations to agree to form an {{LinkCTP1|alliance}}, {{LinkCTP1|attack enemy}}, create a {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}}, or make an {{LinkCTP1|eco pact}}. The following acts of war breaks all treaties and {{LinkCTP1|alliance}}s, which in turn breaks all diplomatic agreements: {{LinkCTP1|Assault}}ing, [[Pillage (CTP1)|Pillaging]], {{LinkCTP1|Bombard}}ing, using a {{LinkCTP1|Nuke}} or {{LinkCTP1|Eco Ranger}} against another Civilization.   ==Great L..."

title: Stop trespass (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Stop trespass''' is a demand that instantly moves the trespasser's units to his closest friendly city if he agrees to the demand. The two Civilizations also agree to a {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} for five turns. Violating this agreement does not break other diplomatic agreements.   ==Great Library entry== People have been trespassing across enemy borders ever since Civilizations first marked borders. Early border markings evolved from colored tree trunks, natural rivers..."

title: Stop trade (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A Civilization can demand another to '''stop trade''' with a third party. In doing this, the two Civilizations also agree to a {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} for five turns.  ==Great Library entry== Treaties have often established the rules of trade between two nations. Sometimes, one nation will require its trading partner to cease trade with its enemy. Using diplomacy in this manner, a nation can weaken its enemy with a pen stroke.  [[Category:Diplomacy (CTP1)]]"

title: Stop piracy (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A Civilization can order another to '''stop all piracy''' of its {{LinkCTP1|trade routes}}. The two Civilizations also agree to a {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} for five turns.  ==Great Library entry== Throughout history, piracy in one form or another has been a bane to governments and individuals alike. The threat of piracy was so great that sometimes routes developed in hostile environments (like the Himalayas) where merchants hoped that the severe territory might discourag..."

title: Reduce pollution (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A Civilization can order another to '''reduce {{LinkCTP1|pollution}}'''. In doing this, the two Civilizations also agree to a {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} for five turns.  ==Great Library entry== Since the 20th century, pollution became a global problem with only global solutions. Air pollution, toxic waste disposal, acid rain, and contaminated water supplies could originate in one nation and contaminate another. To prevent this, nations formed treaties to reduce pollution...."

title: Peace treaty (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Peace treaties''' occur as a result of diplomatic agreements. A peace treaty discourages two Civilizations from attacking one another. If either Civilization does attack, its reputation will be sullied. Violating this agreement breaks all diplomatic agreements.   ==Great Library entry== The peace treaty, a temporary agreement to cease all hostility, has been a very important diplomatic solution to the crisis of war, often used with varying results. For example, during..."

title: Gift (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A Civilization can give a '''gift''' of {{LinkCTP1|gold}}, maps, and {{LinkCTP1|Advances}} to another Civilization. When a Civilization gives a gift, a 5-turn {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} begins between the two Civilizations.  ==Great Library entry== Gifts are often used by nations as an expression of good will and perhaps even more frequently, as a way of coercing nations to support their cause. In sometimes very controversial policies, the United States gives billions of..."

title: Exchange (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Two Civilizations can engage in an '''exchange''' of maps, or, with an embassy, Advances. A 5-turn {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} begins between two Civilizations who engage in an exchange.  ==Great Library entry== Diplomacy often calls for give and take and exchanges between parties. The Louisiana Purchase was one such exchange where France relinquished claim on much of America in return for an astonishingly small $15 million dollars. With this, the young United States doubl..."

title: Establish embassy (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Diplomat}}s can '''establish embassies''' in a foreign cities. Embassies allow the player to view some of the target Civilization's secret information. Establishing embassies is free.  ==Great Library entry== Embassies are important functional and symbolic representations of the mother country. Historically, the establishing of a foreign embassy in a new country has been a gesture of a desire to have working relations with the host country. Home to the Diploma..."

title: Eco pact (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Engaging in an '''eco pact''' forms a treaty between two Civilizations to reduce {{LinkCTP1|pollution}}. The treaty lasts until global pollution is no longer rising.  ==Great Library entry== The health of the environment earned great international attention during the 20th century. Nations banded together at conferences such as the Stockholm Environment Conference in 1972 to ratify treaties that established goals and limits on industrial and population growth. Nations co..."

title: Diplomacy (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Diplomacy''' is the critical system that allows a Civilization to negotiate with other nations it has contacted, thereby improving or destroying relations and gaining desired benefits. Civilizations may make {{LinkCTP1|demand}}s, offer {{LinkCTP1|gift}}s, encourage {{LinkCTP1|exchange}}s, or offer [[treaty (CTP1)|treaties]].  ==Great Library entry== Wise diplomacy has often made the difference between the survival and destruction of a Civilization. Successful Civiliza..."

title: Demand (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Issuing a '''demand''' is a way for a Civilization to request another Civilization to surrender its {{LinkCTP1|gold}}, maps, or to perform an action. With an embassy, a Civilization may also demand {{LinkCTP1|Advances}}. When a Civilization acquiesces to a demand and completes the act requested, a 5-turn {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} begins between the two Civilizations.  ==Great Library entry== While history is replete with tales of war, another story travels through the po..."

title: Attack enemy (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A Civilization can form a treaty with another Civilization to '''attack a third party'''. In forming this treaty, the two Civilizations also agree to a {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}} until the enemy is destroyed.  ==Great Library entry== Historically, nations have allied with one another against common enemies. By agreeing to unify their efforts against a single target such as a city, diplomatic partners could succeed as military victors. In 1939, Russia and Germany signed th..."

title: Alliance (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Alliances''' allow two Civilizations to enjoy a permanent {{LinkCTP1|peace treaty}}. Violating this agreement breaks all diplomatic agreements.   ==Great Library entry== Nations often turn to alliances to accomplish goals beyond the power of a single nation. Even in early times, organizations such as the Delian League of Greece provided mutual protection for like-minded cities. In the 20th century, NATO offered an example of one of the most successful of alliances, sh..."

title: Bombard (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Units with the bombard ability can '''bombard''' once per turn. Bombarding functions as a ranged attack against one unit in the target tile. The bombarding units will not take any damage unless the target tile has a unit capable of counter-bombarding. Bombarding ends the turn for land and sea units. A city may lose 1 population when bombarded.   ==Great Library entry== With the development of fortifications attackers needed new tactics in order to penetrate new defenses...."

title: Assault (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Units can '''assault''' by attempting to move into the tile of the target unit. Assaulting units must have enough movement points to move into the target tile. Land and sea units end their turn after assaulting. Air units can assault and continue to move, but cannot assault twice in one turn. A city may lose 1 population when assaulted, and loses 1 population when captured.  ==Great Library entry== The basic assault, engaging in combat, dates back to before recorded hist..."

title: X-Lab (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Construction of the '''Xenoform Laboratory''' is the first step of the {{LinkCTP1|Alien Life Project}}. If the X-Lab is captured or destroyed, the project is destroyed. It requires a completed {{LinkCTP1|Wormhole}} and {{LinkCTP1|Probe}} mission.  ==Great Library entry== When the first alien artifacts were uncovered on Mars, most of the world's major governments began secret research in the fields of alien biology and communication. New installations were constructed to..."

title: Wormhole (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Wormholes''' occur only in {{LinkCTP1|space}}. The Wormhole becomes visible after the completion of the {{LinkCTP1|Wormhole Sensor}} {{LinkCTP1|Wonder}}. One victory condition requires a Civilization to send a {{LinkCTP1|Wormhole Probe}} into the Wormhole.  ==Great Library entry== Thousands of years ago ancient astrologers wrote about a gleaming purple eye that opened in the heavens when certain stars were properly aligned. Modern astronomers dismissed such legends as..."

title: Gene splicer (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Each '''Gene Splicer''' speeds the alien embryo's growth. The Splicers can be built in any city and will be shipped automatically to the site of the {{LinkCTP1|X-Lab}}. It requires a completed {{LinkCTP1|Wormhole}}, {{LinkCTP1|Probe}} mission and {{LinkCTP1|X-lab}}.  ==Great Library entry== Developed by eugenics researchers in the late 28th century, Gene Splicers were massive machines capable of analyzing, synthesizing, and combining the most complex DNA code sequences...."

title: Fortify (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Units with the '''fortify''' ability can fortify on certain tiles. Fortifying gives a 50% defensive bonus after two turns.  ==Great Library entry== Fortifying, the digging or occupying of a trench for defensive purposes, is a strategy that goes back to before the Romans. Simple fortifications took the form of shallow foxholes, while more elaborate ones involved networked trenches and tunnels with lines of communication and supplies. During the first American Civil War th..."

title: Embryo tank (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Construction of the '''Embryo Tank''' is the second step of the {{LinkCTP1|Alien Life Project}}. The Tank can be built in any city and will be shipped automatically to the site of the {{LinkCTP1|X-Lab}}. It requires a completed {{LinkCTP1|Wormhole}}, {{LinkCTP1|Probe}} mission and {{LinkCTP1|X-lab}}.  ==Great Library entry== Combining the latest advances in recombinant DNA engineering and enhanced incubation, prototype embryo tanks had been used to grow full human clones..."

title: ECD (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A minimum of two additional '''ECD''' devices are required to proceed to each new stage of the Alien's development. After six ECD's have been built, any additional ECD results in a bonus added to the player's score. The ECD's can be built in any city and will be shipped automatically to the site of the {{LinkCTP1|X-Lab}}.  ==Great Library entry== The Extraterrestrial Communication Device was an advanced biological computer designed by scientists at the Center for Psychic..."

title: Disband unit (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "As technology improves, fighting forces must upgrade their equipment and training to keep competitive in the field of battle. A unit may return to any {{LinkCTP1|city}} and '''disband''' to contribute half of its {{LinkCTP1|production}} cost back to the city in order to produce a contemporary item.  ==Great Library entry== During the 20th century, nations competed in an arms race that drove the development of progressively more advanced military units. Rather than pay fo..."

title: Disband city (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "A Player can '''disband a {{LinkCTP1|city}}''' of three population or less. This destroys the city. Players receive a {{LinkCTP1|Settler}} for disbanding a city and there is no score penalty for this act.   ==Great Library entry== Not all Cities are built to last. Many large settlements, like the boom towns of the American West or the military bases of World War II, are abandoned once the usefulness of their location has expired. When such a city is vacated, the final re..."

title: Containment field (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "At each stage of the embryo's development, there is a small chance of a cataclysmic failure resulting in the destruction of the entire project. Building extra '''Containment Field''' units helps to reduce this risk. The Fields can be built in any city and will be shipped automatically to the site of the {{LinkCTP1|X-Lab}}.  *One field = 20% failure chance per stage *Two fields = 10% failure chance per stage *Three fields = full protection  ==Great Library entry== After s..."

title: Veterans (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Military Units can become '''veterans''' by winning battles. When a unit achieves veteran status, it receives a 50% bonus to its assault statistic when attacking.   ==Great Library entry== Veteran units are battle-hardened troops whose combat experience gives them added strength and cunning. From the Auxillarium legion of ancient Rome to the SS Panzer divisions of WWII, veteran units have determined the outcome of many major battles.  [[Category:Game concepts (CTP1)]]"

title: Unload (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Unload allows''' you to move loaded units from a transport into a neighboring tile. However, only the {{LinkCTP1|Marine}}, {{LinkCTP1|Storm Marine}} and {{LinkCTP1|Swarm}} can unload into enemy occupied tiles.  ==Great Library entry== Historically, ships and other vehicles have been critical for their use as transports, vehicles in which to move military and civilian units. In ancient times warriors sailed to battle in oar-driven Triremes. Over time the vehicles used..."

title: Sue (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Lawyer}s} '''sue''' other {{LinkCTP1|trade units}} like Lawyers and Corporate Branches, which destroys them. In addition, the Lawyer can sue franchised cities to remove the franchise. The attack costs 500 gold and always succeeds.  ==Great Library entry== Towards the end of the 20th century the lawsuit became an increasingly popular means of attack in both political and private conflicts. As international laws assumed greater authority, skilled lawyers waged b..."

title: Steal advance (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "[[Spy (CTP1)|Spies]] and {{LinkCTP1|Cyber Ninja}}s can target a city to steal an {{LinkCTP1|advance}} from another Civilization. A Spy has a 50% chance of success along with a 50% chance of being caught and killed if the attempt fails. A Cyber Ninja carries a 50% chance of success as well as a lesser, 25% chance of being caught and killed should her attempt fail. Additionally, both units can try to steal a specific advance, however, their chances of success decrease shou..."

title: Spy (concept) (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Diplomat}}s, [[Spy (CTP1)|Spies]] and {{LinkCTP1|Cyber Ninja}}s can '''spy''' on a foreign {{LinkCTP1|city}} to reveal the city's vital statistics. Diplomats have a 75% success rate and a 100% chance of being captured if they fail. Spies have a 75% success rate and a 50% chance of being captured if they fail. Cyber Ninjas have a 75% success rate and a 25% chance of being captured if they fail. The espionage screen can be reviewed within the same turn by right-..."

title: Special forces (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Special forces''' units are generally unconventional units engaged in different forms of covert warfare or else professional military units. Some military units are also Special Forces, ready to strike at a moment's notice. All Special Forces are always considered "At War" in regard to {{LinkCTP1|Military Readiness}}.  ==Great Library entry== Throughout history, military forces relied on civilian conscripts, often yanked forcibly from their homes and farms to fight fo..."

title: Soothsay (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Cleric}}s and {{LinkCTP1|Televangelist}}s can '''soothsay''', which spreads 5 unhappiness in a target {{LinkCTP1|city}}. The attack always succeeds and costs 500 gold.  ==Great Library entry== Soothsaying, the foretelling of future events, serves as a tool used by religious fanatics and doomsayers to spread the word of imminent Armageddon, and thereby encourages people to seek salvation - quickly. By predicting dire events, soothsaying spreads discontent. Whil..."

title: Sleep (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Sleep''' allows you to put your units to sleep rendering them temporarily inactive. Sleeping units are ignored by the Next Unit button. Sleeping units awake when the enemy moves to an adjacent tile.  [[Category:Game concepts (CTP1)]]"

title: Settle (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Settler}}s, {{LinkCTP1|Sea Engineer}}s, and {{LinkCTP1|Space Engineer}}s can build a {{LinkCTP1|city}} or colony. After this, the Settler is removed and becomes the first citizen.  ==Great Library entry== Since the beginning of time man has pushed forward, crossing into hostile, lonely territory where he has settled, establishing a home, a family, a business: forming the seeds of a future city. In the early stages of Civilization as nomads learned to domestica..."

title: Sell indulgence (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Cleric}}s and {{LinkCTP1|Televangelist}}s can '''sell indulgences''', which adds {{LinkCTP1|happiness}} while draining gold from the target {{LinkCTP1|city}}, and sending it to the attacking Civilization. This attack is always successful and it's free.  ==Great Library entry== Historically, religions have depended on charitable contributions for sustenance and growth. In Western Europe the Catholic church was notorious for its form of acquiring funds. One of t..."

title: Reform city (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Units with the reform ability can '''reform a {{LinkCTP1|city}}''', which causes 5 unhappiness while removing conversion. Reforming costs 1,000 gold.  ==Great Library entry== There is a long tradition of governments or religions using oppressive techniques to crush opposition, particularly religious opposition. One of the most famous crackdowns, The Spanish Inquisition (which actually swept most of Europe), forced people through often brutal means to bow before the power..."

title: Plant nuke (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "[[Spy (CTP1)|Spies]] and {{LinkCTP1|Cyber Ninja}}s can plant a Nuke in a foreign {{LinkCTP1|city}}. The saboteur and all units surrounding the city die along with a large number of the city's population. The Spy has a 25% chance of success, and a 50% chance of being caught and execeuted for the crime. Cyber Ninjas succeed 25% of the time with a 25% chance of being caught and executed.  ==Great Library entry== The nuclear weapon has been one of the most terrifying weapons..."

title: Piracy (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "'''Piracy''' allows a Civilization to destroy an enemy's {{LinkCTP1|trade route}} and make a buck in the bargain. Piraters gain 30 gold - although this is not guaranteed. Watch out though. This is sure to anger other Civilizations.  ==Great Library entry== Throughout history, piracy in one form or another has been a bane to governments and individuals alike. The threat of piracy was so great that sometimes routes developed in hostile environments (like the Himalayas) whe..."

title: Pillage (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "Military land units can '''pillage''' and completely destroy an enemy's {{LinkCTP1|tile improvement}}s or installations.  ==Great Library entry== Throughout history Civilizations have often pillaged their conquered enemy, stealing valuables, destroying places of worship, and leaving behind smoldering ruins. Although most armies engaged in this ruthless act, the barbarians are famous for their rampant looting. The Vandals and the Visigoths both pillaged Rome, signaling th..."

title: Paradrop (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Paratrooper}}s can '''paradrop''' on a target within 20 tiles using a transport. Paradrops must originate in a {{LinkCTP1|city}} or from an {{LinkCTP1|Air Base}}.  ==Great Library entry== Beginning with WWII, infantry gained tremendous mobility by parachuting into target zones. Soldiers could paradrop behind enemy lines as a small force meant to infiltrate, or paratroopers could deploy en masse. On June 6, 1944 over ten thousand paratroopers landed in German-o..."

title: Nano-attack (CTP1)
comment: Created page with "{{LinkCTP1|Ecoterrorist}}s can '''nano-attack''', which destroys all {{LinkCTP1|city improvement}}s in the infected {{LinkCTP1|city}}. Any city trading with the infected city has a 20% chance of becoming infected in the next turn. The Ecoterrorist has a 25% chance of success. However, if the attack fails the Ecoterrorist also has a 25% chance of being caught and killed. The nano-attack costs 4,000 gold.   ==Great Library entry== Starting in 2112 Ecoterrorists programmed..."

comment: Created page with "When the player achieves a sufficiently good score, he will be presented with the '''Monuments Screen'''.
